args.part: Three lobe fidget spinner with print-in-place hub
assumptions: Three lobes at 90, 210 and 330 degrees, tip radius 37.5 mm (75 mm across), valleys near 22.5 mm radius.
Spinner body sits 0.4 mm above the base disk (z 2.4 to 10.4) and the cap sits 0.4 mm above the body, so all parts print separated.
The pin rises from the base disk through the bore; the bore is 0.4 mm larger per side than the pin.
The base disk is a print anchor only; it can be removed later if it is not wanted.
PLA on the P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle.
questions: Should the lobes be fully round or sharper at the tips?

steps.text:
I built the three lobe fidget spinner as one design, and it passes the plan check: watertight, minimum wall 2 mm.

It has five features: a 20 mm base disk, an 8 mm fixed pin, the 8 mm thick spinner body, an 8.8 mm bore through the hub, and a 12 mm retaining cap on the pin top. The body sits 0.4 mm above the base and 0.4 mm below the cap, so it can spin freely without a bearing.

- **Size:** I read "75 mm across" as the tip radius (37.5 mm) setting the outer size. The actual bounding box is 67 by 63.5 mm, because the three tips are not diametrically opposite.
- **Guessed sizes:** the hub, bore, pin, base, cap and 0.4 mm gap were my guesses, and you confirmed them on the sheet.
- **Base disk:** it is only there to anchor the pin during printing. You can remove it later if you do not want it.

I have not sliced or sent anything to the printer. The next step would be to slice it on your P1S with PLA at 0.4 mm and queue it for approval. Want me to do that?
